compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: The disciples puzzle over “a little while”; Jesus compares sorrow turning to joy with childbirth, speaks of direct asking and the Father’s love, predicts scattering, and locates peace in himself amid oppression.
observations.label: Sorrow turns to joy before scattering and peace

observations.body: The passage presents Asking, speaking plainly, scattering, and leaving as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Asking, speaking plainly, scattering, and leaving

observations.body: The passage places Sorrow turned to joy beside Asking, speaking plainly, scattering, and leaving.
observations.label: Sorrow turned to joy

payload.posture: Read John 16:16–33 as one movement in the Last Supper, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.title: Sorrow turns to joy before scattering and peace
